gapA_origin.finding: the night origin, not the arm, is the uncontrolled phase term
gapA_origin.cause: apps/device/src/modern-campaign-ports.js supplies the executor's `observe` as lifecycle(), which runs a full `adb exec-out screencap -p` at 2400x1080 into tools/device/lifecycle-observe.py on every poll. The executor's own poll interval is 250 ms, so the ~1.7 s residual is the capture-and-classify round trip, not the schedule.
gapA_origin.why it governs: the model's response to delivered phase repeats on a 1000 ms game second and loses on [116.67,166.67), [316.67,366.67), [416.67,800) and [916.67,966.67) -- 53.3% of phases. A 1852 ms bracket is wider than the whole period, so the delivered phase is unconstrained and the model's own uncontrolled-phase result, 1375/3000, is the ceiling for any arm mode until the origin is pinned.
gapA_origin.candidate: the native Cue Helper read already reports screen=FNAF2_NIGHT with a visualCaptureAt timestamp and visualCaptureUncertaintyMs 0 at ~43 ms detector latency, and the executor already calls it for control-effect sampling. Pinning the ORIGIN from that stream while leaving the Python lifecycle classifier as the AUTHORITY on whether a night is running respects the rule that a detector which knows one way to be dead must not be what says you are alive. Not implemented; not measured on device.
gapA_origin.secondOriginPath: the 2026-09-12T00-50 run stamped hid.night-go with source `intro-handoff`, not `lifecycle`: in shared mode startSharedSchedule() records the origin from the handoff request instead. There are therefore TWO origin paths and the refinement added in this session covers only the lifecycle one. Which path a run takes was not predicted in advance and is itself open.

gapB_acceptance.finding: one steady-loop press is systematically not accepted by the game; a second apparent miss was the OBSERVER being blind and is retracted

systematicMisses.precededBy: toys-6 monitorUp->false at plan offset 14000, i.e. 400 ms earlier
systematicMisses.backing: the mask rule positively read maskOn=true 17 times elsewhere in the same run (34 true reads across all samples), so it demonstrably can see the state it graded MISSING here

gapB_acceptance.caveat: MISSING means the target state was positively not observed. That is only evidence of a lost press when the grading rule has shown it can read that state at all, so run-report.mjs now qualifies every systematic miss by the rule's positive-read count in the same run and marks the rest UNPROVEN-OBSERVER-BLIND.
gapB_acceptance.candidate: for the surviving miss, the mask seam is the standing explanation (tools/device/actuator.mjs SEAM_BANDS). `loopContactMs: 200` is flagged in minus-toys-plan.mjs KNOBS0 as the experiment worth running because every parity inversion repaired on 2026-09-09 was a 33 ms tap; it gates 3000/3000 normal and worst on night 5, as does maskOffMs=9050 with raiseMs=10250, and so does the combination. None is bound to a qualification and none is tested on device.

retractedMisses.reason: the monitor rule read monitorUp=true only 2 times in 266 samples across this run, while the schedule raised the monitor 6 times and the recording shows the camera feed up. Its MISSING rows are the rule failing to see a raised monitor, not the press being lost. modern-campaign-ports.js already records the same blindness on Night 5 (campaign-2026-09-09T14-14-39: 41 observations, 40 false, 1 true). This was first written up here as an actuator gap and is retracted.

delivery.finding: the device-local stream itself does not drift
delivery.detail: all 25 graded transitions carry a contactAt exactly on the planned offset from hid.night-go (delta +0 ms through 54.4 s). That is the scheduler's computed contact time, not a measured landing, so it proves the stream carried no internal drift and proves nothing about what the game received. Acceptance is graded separately above.

retractions: An earlier statement in this session that Night 5 tolerates at most 408 ms of arm-release lag was WRONG. It came from tools/device/minus-toys-margin.mjs's edge() scan, which stops at the first failure and is only valid for a contiguous basin. The response is banded and periodic, so 408 ms is one band edge and not a budget: the model scores 3000/3000 at 800-1400 ms of lag. The margin tool now reports bands and refuses the single-number reading, and phase-reconstruct.mjs's model.lossBands was already the authority.

An earlier version of THIS record named `toys-3 monitorUp->true` as a systematic actuator gap. It is retracted: the monitor rule is near-blind to a raised monitor on this night, so the MISSING rows are observation failure. The instrument was changed rather than only the text -- run-report.mjs now refuses to call a miss systematic unless the same rule positively read that target state at least 5 times in the same run.
